subject: Chemistry
title: Nucleophilic Addition to the Carbonyl Group
summary: Most reactions of aldehydes and ketones begin with one move. How a nucleophile attacks the polar C=O, and why aldehydes react faster than ketones.

notes.title: 06 – Nucleophilic Addition to the Carbonyl Group

keyPoints: The C=O bond is **polar**: carbon is delta plus, oxygen delta minus.
A **nucleophile** attacks the electrophilic carbon; the pi electrons move onto oxygen.
The carbon changes from **sp² (flat)** to **sp³ (tetrahedral)**, giving an **alkoxide intermediate**.
The intermediate takes a **proton** to give the product: HCN gives a **cyanohydrin**.
**Aldehydes react faster than ketones**: less crowding, and a more positive carbon.

rows: One alkyl group and a small H: easy to reach
One electron-releasing group: carbon more positive
Two electron-releasing groups: carbon less positive
